title: Move over Gamescom, Konami is heading to CatCon and its bringing Metal Gear Solid-themed cat toys with it
summary: Cats vs snakes—a rivalry as old as time.
body: Have you ever looked at your cat and thought, 'I bet they'd love Metal Gear Solid'. Well, if you have, then not only does your cat have impeccable taste, but you can share in the hobby with these new MGS-themed cat toys. Just not at Gamescom. No, unfortunately, for everyone wandering through the Koelnmesse right now, Konami is bringing its set of MGS cat gear to CatCon 2026 instead, the "world's largest cat-centric pop-up event—ok, I guess that makes more sense than Cologne. Fans will be able to pick up plushie pet toys, cat collars inspired by Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker and Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots , and scratch boxes both online and at the booth from October 10-11. (Image credit: Konami Digital Entertainment) But those who make it to the booth will also get the added benefit of meeting Uno the one-eared cat, who Konami aptly names a 'cat-fluencer'. I'm not the biggest fan of influencers, but I'll make an exception for Uno because she looks very polite. "Uno and Kat featured in a special playthrough video of Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2 where they revealed the specialty cardboard cat boxes." I don't even have a cat and I want to get one of these—…

title: Micron, the trillion-dollar memory company, refused to replace a crucial drive for current market value until Reddit got mad
summary: 'Pushing back actually worked.'
body: With the memory crisis only continuing to get worse, a PC gamer's fear right now is likely their memory, storage or GPU borking, and needing to spend an inflated price to replace it. One such Redditor had an external drive die in just one year, and Crucial only offered a refund of the original price they paid, which was a lot less than similar drives go for now. That was until they brought their problems to Reddit. Over on the PCMR subreddit , user CarefulMeasurement99 shared that they bought a 4 TB Crucial drive a year ago for $200, and when it broke, Crucial offered that original price in a refund. That same drive seems to fetch up to $800 now (thanks, AI). Crucial originally set up an RMA for the drive in order to pick it up and send it back to the company. The Redditor replied to this saying, "Due to the recent global increase in SSD prices, $199.999 is unfortunately no longer enough to purchase a new 4 TB drive in the current market", and officially requested a direct replacement. This story gets a tad complicated because Micron announced the closure of the Crucial consumer business late last year, which threw its ability to actually replace the drive into question. title: Star Wars Zero Company review
summary: Getting tactical with the boys.
body: NEED TO KNOW What is it Star Wars XCOM, but even better than that sounds. Release date August 27, 2026 Expect to pay $50/£40 Publisher Disney / EA / Respawn / Lucasfilm Developer Bit Reactor Reviewed on Core i5 12600K, RX 9070 XT, 32 GB RAM Multiplayer None Steam Deck Not Likely Link Steam It's kinda weird that it took somebody this long to make a Star Wars squad tactics game, but studio Bit Reactor has, for all intents and purposes, knocked it outta da park. Star Wars Zero Company is a superbly executed⁠—if familiar⁠—tactics game, but it's also a new all-timer Star Wars story: I'm talking Rogue One, Knights of the Old Republic, TIE Fighter-tier. Melt away everything else, and it's got a Terminator skeleton of pure XCOM, the trendsetting tactics series many of Bit Reactor's senior developers cut their teeth on. But the studio struck out from there into more uncharted territory: lavish production values, zoomed-in action game-style exploration, and some truly knockout set pieces and story beats. title: Rockstar responds to GTA 6 leaks: 'This is not how we intended for you see the game after all this time'
summary: The studio has described the leaks as "heartbreaking for our team".
body: The news cycle this past week has been dominated with Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, and for good reason, Rockstar studios has sprung a big one, with the self-ordained "Cyberleek" drumming up attention with waves of public manifestos, statements, and a little crypto farming on the side. In preparation for its somewhat-confusing Netflix-exclusive gameplay reveal tomorrow, Rockstar's finally acknowledged the leaks. Both confirming that they're real beyond a shadow of a doubt (not that there was much doubt to begin with), and trying to salvage some hype. "We know that many of you have been waiting to hear from us regarding the events of the past week," reads a post to Rockstar's Instagram . "It would be an understatement to say that having videos of Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay leak in this way has been heartbreaking for our team, and this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time. "We are very sorry that everything has taken as long as it has—from getting the game finished (nearly there!) to sharing more details and official gameplay, and providing the community with everything you want to know." I'm not sure Rockstar needs to apologise for a videogame t…

summary: Kliff climbing.
body: Crimson Desert didn't get its jaws into me as deep as I'd hoped—partially because of its somewhat scattershot, overwhelming nature . This is purely a matter of personal taste, mind. title: OLED gaming monitors have finally gotten so good that a Counter-Strike 2 tournament is using one
summary: The Asus ROG Swift OLED PG259QWS Ace is the first OLED to make it into a CS2 Major.
body: I've been watching the ascent of OLED with a very keen eye, primarily because as a Counter-Strike 2 gamer, I know just how promising OLEDs will be for competitive gaming. And now it seems we're at the point where they've gotten good enough in specific ways to be the official panel tech of choice in an official CS2 Major tournament. Asus' new monitor, the ROG Swift OLED PG259QWS Ace , is going to be the official monitor of the 2026 PGL CS2 major . It's a glossy tandem WOLED with a response time of 0.02 ms (GTG), which is low even for OLED. More relevant here, though, is that it's a 720 Hz, 24.5-inch panel. We've seen high refresh rate OLEDs before, but most of these (A) are 27-inch or bigger, and (B) only achieve their high refresh rates when dropped to 720p. Getting up to 1080p is ideal for pro gaming, especially in CS2, where some will want to stretch a 4:3 resolution, and 24/25-inch monitors are preferred. It might seem silly to some, but I've tested some pro-level monitors and can confirm that 24/25-inch monitors can make playing CS2 a little more comfortable, allowing you to see the entire game scene without squinting in a way that pushing a 27-inch monitor further away someho…

title: We saw The Witcher 3 – Songs of the Past in action, and the full-game remaster that's coming this year too
summary: Just when he thought he was out, Songs of the Past pulls Geralt back in.
body: In Print This is a shorter version of an exclusive Witcher 3 – Songs of the Past cover feature that will go out in the next issue of PC Gamer magazine . Keep your eyes peeled! Surprise! Songs of the Past, The Witcher 3's third expansion, isn't kicked off by some Ciri-centric weft in the space-time continuum, nor another curt and urgent letter from Yennefer. As for Triss, well, I didn't spot a single red hair of her in the hands-off demo that CD Projekt Red and Fool's Theory gave us. It's Dandelion. Geralt's lute-plucking biographer has gone missing, and who better to find him than his best pal in the whole wide world? So when Songs of the Past releases next year, he'll be back on the path in a region of The Witcher's world we've never seen before—Dandelion's family home of Letten, in the kingdom of Redania. And he's got another surprise for you, too: a full Witcher 3 remaster that aims to make the 2015 classic feel like it released in the modern era, due for release on September 29. Over a decade since The Witcher 3's last expansion, the boys are back in town. There's No Place Like Where better to get a glimpse of Dandelion's true face than his family home? title: Metro 2039 takes us back to Moscow, but it's still got some delicious bits of Exodus in there
summary: Delicious up until you realise you've wasted all your gas mask juice trying to open a closet door.
body: Isn't it always the way? You spend so long yearning to leave home, to strike out and make a go of it all by yourself, but the second you step foot out the door you start missing it. All of it. The camaraderie and the rows, the shared meals and the constant, privacy-smothering proximity, and—of course—the mutated beasts from the overland, intent on your complete and utter destruction. This is how I imagine it went for 4A Games when it came time to make Metro 2039 , the fourth mainline game in the Metro series. Artyom is gone—he took a train off into Russia's carcass in Exodus, but Moscow and its metro endure, and 4A has returned to them for 2039. In Artyom's absence, you play someone new: The Stranger, a gruff and—in contrast to the previous three Metros—chatty protagonist who's on a quest to find and kill Hunter, the former legendary Ranger hero and (it seems) current overlord of almost the entire metro. Things have gone to pot since Artyom went interrailing. The metro's many fractious stations have largely been brought under one banner, but it is a fascist banner, ruled over by Hunter with an iron fist. Someone should probably put an end to that. title: Ubisoft forgot to make sure the Steam release of Heroes of Might & Magic 3 included the actual game
summary: Oops.
body: The HD rerelease of Heroes of Might & Magic 3 from 2015 used to be the only way to get the strategy classic on Steam, leaving many players frustrated since it lacked the expansions and the random map generator. Ask fans of the series, and they'd tell you to get the original version from GOG instead. So it should be an easy win for Ubisoft that the series' current owner finally decided to put the original version, complete with its expansions Armageddon's Blade and The Shadow of Death, on Steam at last. Its current user review rating of 80% negative suggests otherwise. Fork out $10 for it and you'll find an install that's only 23.49 KB big, which gives a "dummy executable" error message when you try to launch it. Because Heroes of Might & Magic 3 on Steam does not come with Heroes of Might & Magic 3. Somebody forgot to include the actual game files with the game. I'm sure this will be fixed soon, perhaps when France wakes up, but in the meantime the complete edition on GOG is still the best version and it's currently on sale for half-price . body: While gameplay footage of the upcoming D&D game shows off a solo warlock , if you'd like to play a warlock as a member of a classic party of adventurers then Solasta 2's next update has got your back. Early access update 1 will add the warlock class and two subclasses (the timekeeper and the dreamer), as well as co-op multiplayer. Up to four people will be able to join the same multiplayer session, whether starting a new game or joining one already in progress. The host can assign a new player an existing character, or they can bring an existing one, or create a new one on the spot. Control of companions who join your party can also be split up as you go. Every player gets a vote on the big story and dialogue choices, and there's a ping system being added to help you communicate. body: It brings me no joy to admit this, but recently I've begun thinking that I'm finally nearing my fill of ARPGs. Or at least that's what I thought until roughly 45 minutes ago, when I saw the announcement trailer for Tarae: The Unbound that had been slipped into a Gamescom 2026 Opening Night Live Montage. (Image credit: Krafton) The problem, I now realize, is that I've mostly spent my time with ARPGs looking at the same kinds of things. Most games downstream of Diablo tend to flow into the same basin of interchangeable demons, dark cultists, and piles of weird meat. But looking at the brief clips of Tarae, I realize now I'd just been aching for a jolt to the ARPG aesthetic palette. Developed by Boundary and published by Krafton, Tarae's Steam page says it's set in "a world that reimagines Eastern myth, folklore, and traditional aesthetics, where beauty and mystery are entwined with darkness and brutality." title: Paradox's next grand strategy game is taking cues from Fallout and Mad Max
summary: Afterworld will let you conquer post-apocalyptic North America.
body: Paradox Development Studio is taking a break from conquering history and space, setting its sights instead on post-apocalyptic North America. Afterworld will see you take control of a tribe of survivors as you explore and conquer the ruins of the fallen continent. Which you might already know, after yesterday's leak. But now it's official! Afterworld was just revealed during Gamescom's Opening Night Live, with a trailer that's evocative of both Fallout and Mad Max. Paradox has naturally put its own spin on things, however, with features like the Ancients, immortal leaders who existed before the collapse of civilisation, and who are now fighting to rule what's left using forgotten technology. They might cause some problems for you. Like Stellaris, you'll be able to pick your tribe's origins, including a Fallout-inspired start that sees you leaving the safety of your bunker to begin a new life in the wasteland. There's a survival bent to the proceedings, with your tribe needing to scrounge up the bare necessities like food and water before it can start thriving. title: The hardware crisis has hit a new low: We're now using rats for RAM
summary: Rat computer.
body: Good news from the near future: Space travel has apparently advanced enough to allow humanity to establish a hotel on the surface of the moon. Bad news: The RAMpocalypse apparently continues unabated, forcing novel experimentation with alternate forms of computer memory not rendered wholly unaffordable by AI datacenters. Namely, rat computers. This believable projection of the current miserable state of consumer hardware comes courtesy of Ontos, the next game from Amnesia developer Frictional Games. In the trailer above, a man strapped to a chair with electrodes stuck in his head is a bit freaky, though less so than another guy who's missing everything from his upper teeth down; perhaps humanity in the future is so desperate for localized processing power that we're resorting to shoving DisplayPort cables into our brains, too. The strongest big of imagery in the trailer by far, though, is a computer the size of a wall with 60 rats connected to it in sequence. Or parallel? I'm not great on my circuitry fundamentals, but I know a rat computer when I see one. I am instinctively scared of the rat computer and the unknown potential of 60 rat minds taking the place of random access asia…

title: The Witcher 3 Remastered announced: another huge free update, and all Witcher 3 owners get the existing expansions free
summary: The update isn't just graphical, and it's out in September.
body: The Witcher 3 got a "Next-Gen Update" back in 2022, and CD Projekt Red is doing it again: The developer announced at Gamescom today that The Witcher 3 Remastered is coming September 29 as a free update for all owners of the RPG. Aside from graphical updates (of which there are many), The Witcher 3 Remastered makes changes to combat, movement, Roach riding, monster behaviors, the skill tree, and the photo mode. The kicker: Alongside the update, owners of The Witcher 3 will also get its two expansions, Blood and Wine and Hearts of Stone, free if they don't already own them. For newcomers, the expansions will be bundled with The Witcher 3 Remastered. The remaster arrives well in advance of the next expansion, Songs of the Past , which releases sometime next year. "My favorite [new feature] is the visuals. That's new textures, updated rendering, advanced path tracing, foliage, you name it," said CD Projekt Red level design lead Miles Tost at Gamescom's Opening Night Live showcase. "Geralt has never looked this good, even after all those years of retirement. "And then the other thing, definitely, is combat. It's more modern, smooth and precise. title: Lego is finally fulfilling its destiny by making a city builder
summary: Took you long enough.
body: In retrospect I'm not sure why it's taken Lego so long to get here: it's made Star Wars games, Batman games... heck, it even made a Fortnite game. The first Lego videogame came out way back in 1997! But at least it's finally fulfilling its destiny: The blocks that were made for building are finally being used for a city builder. Lego Skylines was announced today at Gamescom, and yeah, it looks like the perfect fit. Have a peek at the announcement below. Looks pretty darn sweet, and looks pretty darn big. But how big? "In this cozy, customizable city-builder, your choices bring a living, breathing metropolis to life. Go big or obsess over the details. No instructions. Unlimited space," says Paradox Interactive. Unlimited space? For real? That's... quite a lot of space. "Remember hospitals to keep everyone in one piece. Wheat for the donuts. Garbage collection, sewage, and all the other things that make a city click. How it all comes together is up to you. So stick your hard hat on and greenlight your weirdest ideas," Paradox says. Sounds good to me: it's got that Lego cuteness but also looks like it doesn't skimp on the complexity. Interestingly, Lego Skylines is being developed by…

title: Path of Exile 2 is finally getting swords in December, and also the rest of the game
summary: Grinding Gear Games squeezes one more class in before the action RPG leaves early access and goes free-to-play.
body: It's finally time for the one thing every Path of Exile 2 player has been waiting for: swords. A new class and weapon type is coming to the action RPG later this year—oh, and the full 1.0 release of the game. On December 11, PoE 2 will leave early access behind and go full free-to-play, just like its predecessor. While developer Grinding Gear Games has several previously announced classes to get to eventually, the 1.0 release will at least include the one many players have been waiting for. The Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026 trailer doesn't actually give the man with the sword a title, but a post on the GGG forums calls him the duelist, which lines up with the class that was teased a while ago. It's possible he's gone through a few iterations over the last few years, but he's definitely using a sword for all the new skills. Swords are a big deal in PoE 2 because weapons are class agnostic, meaning a new weapon type is like getting a big drop of new skills for everyone to play with. I'm more of a caster player, but I can't deny how good some of them look. title: Atari is taking another shot at reviving RollerCoaster Tycoon
summary: RollerCoaster Tycoon Wonderworks is being developed by Springloaded, makers of the excellent Let's Build a Zoo.
body: Last we saw RollerCoaster Tycoon it was in pretty rickety shape. More than a decade after RollerCoaster Tycoon 3, the follow-up—RollerCoaster Tycoon World—was released to nearly universally poor reviews. Even worse, in one of the all-time dick moves in gaming industry history, Atari launched it exactly one day before rival sim Planet Coaster was due to release. Wow. That nakedly desperate move didn't help the situation: people liked Planet Coaster and didn't like RCTW, and the Tycoon series has been silent since 2016. But here we are another decade later, and Atari is bringing RollerCoaster Tycoon back yet again—though I'm already feeling more hopeful about it. RollerCoaster Tycoon Wonderworks was announced at Gamescom today, and the new entry in the series is being developed by Springloaded, who made the excellent Let's Build a Zoo and is releasing promising gamedev sim Let's Build a Dungeon later this year. That's a good sign, at least! There's no date on the books yet, and RollerCoaster Tycoon Wonderworks won't be feature complete when it launches: it's "coming soon" to early access. Here's its page on Steam .

title: Battle royale goes grunge: there's a new PUBG game and it's set in the '90s
summary: PUBG: Ded.net is "a new multiplayer FPS that combines shooter gameplay with roguelite progression across runs."
body: No one is safe from '90s nostalgia, not even battle royale. A new PUBG game was announced today at Gamescom, and it's gone grunge, according to publisher Krafton. Maybe more interestingly, PUBG: Ded.net is also a roguelite, with progression across runs. Take a peek at the announcement trailer below, set to Ministry's "Jesus Built My Hotrod" (though that's industrial, not grunge) and then come back for some more details. "PUBG: DED.NET is a new multiplayer FPS that combines shooter gameplay with roguelite progression across runs, giving players new ways to experiment, adapt and build their own approach in the strange and unpredictable world of 1990’s Cascadia," says publisher Krafton. title: The next game from Hoyoverse sure looks like someone put Elden Ring's clothes on Monster Hunter

body: As the opening reveal of this year's Gamescom Opening Night Live, HoYoverse brought its first official look at Nodusfall—a change of pace for the gacha game behemoth that looks a little bit Elden Ring, a lot bit Monster Hunter, and a whole pile of proper nouns added for good measure. While I like to think it takes more to catch my attention than forcefully mashing together two things I think are neat, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't tempted by the idea. If there's one thing Monster Hunter monsters have been missing, it's FromSoft-style primordial depression. From the looks of things, there's more than enough metaphysical malaise to go around in Nodusfall. The laws of divinity have apparently frayed, plunging creation into a state of cosmic disarray. There are 10 suns now. Ideally, there's only supposed to be one of those. Not great! Luckily for those of us who like to be given an excuse to try to fight a lizard 30 times our size, all that profound devastation seems to have produced a wide selection of giant, charismatic creatures to swordfight alongside your friends. body: If you remember, uh, yesterday, then you'll remember how I have recently modded GTA 5 to essentially deactivate friction on all NPC cars. In practice, that means driving to a place, picking a guy up, then driving that guy to another place. At some point in this process you lose the cops. All well and good, but not overly dramatic. title: DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction is a definite improvement but path traced fidelity is still not a 100% solved issue
summary: Nvidia has rounded out the DLSS 4.5 stack… now where's DLSS 5?
body: Nvidia's new DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction feature is laser-focused on trying to fix the second most annoying thing about ray traced or path traced games: visual artifacting. Yes, the lighting effect does deliver the most accurate-looking lighting and shadows in games, but in motion there is a definite visual weirdness added into scenes. And that weirdness generally comes from the denoising pass designed to turn the low-fidelity path traced image, with its limited number of rays, into a fully realised frame. Leave a game's viewport still and the scene will pretty rapidly come together to make a sharp, convincing image. Shift that around, or have that scene filled with moving objects or characters and you're going to see the sort of visual trails you might only have been used to in the warehouse parties of your early twenties. Just me? The issue is that it's way too expensive in terms of raw compute to trace every single photon/pixel that would otherwise make up a fully traced scene. Even with the current method of tracking a far smaller representative sample of rays bouncing around the geometry of your game world it's still incredibly demanding of your PC's hardware. title: Hideo Kojima wants to 'continue to focus on making games' at 63, even as 'the time I have decreases'
summary: "I need to constantly scrutinize how I use my time and how I live my life."
body: It's often said that time comes for us all—and while it may not yet be at the doorstep of one Hideo Kojima, he's grown introspective about the prospect on social media after turning 63 over the weekend. In case you've somehow not heard of the man, he's the mind behind the Metal Gear series and Death Stranding. "I've turned 63," Kojima posted to X . "As I get older, the things I 'have to do' and the things I 'want to do' keep increasing. On the other hand, the 'time I have' decreases. I need to constantly scrutinize how I use my time and how I live my life." It's a particularly nostalgic date for Kojima, however, as 2026 also "marks the 40th anniversary of when I started making games, and the 10th anniversary of Kojima Productions." To celebrate, he intends to hold an exhibition at Tokyo's Azabudai Hills Gallery starting at the end of October and lasting until the end of the year. To those fearing his flooded schedule and nostalgic thoughts might precede a retirement from games, though, rest easy. It's just as well then that Be Quiet! is back with a welcome update to the very nearly silent keyboard I loved last year, the Light Mount . As someone with a perennially messy desk, the Light Mount TKL's 80% size is just right; I have room to swish my mouse, and I find I'm not forever accidentally hitting the capslock key as with other cut-down keebs. This TKL update offers more than just a smaller form factor, though, introducing the next generation of Be Quiet!'s Silent switches in Linear and Tactile flavours. title: A disturbing '90s point-and-click horror game about waking up in a rundown asylum with no recollection of who you are is getting a glow up in 2026
summary: Sanitarium probably doesn't need a new version, but it's getting one anyway.
body: 1998 was a vintage year for PC gaming: Half-Life, Unreal, StarCraft, Thief and Baldur's Gate all released in lavish oversize retail boxes, and it was just as busy in console land: Ocarina of Time and Banjo-Kazooie released on Nintendo 64, while the original PlayStation enjoyed Metal Gear Solid and Resident Evil 2. Into this crowd of future classics was also Sanitarium, which shuffled onto shelves, probably sheepishly, in April 1998. It's an isometric point-and-click adventure starring Max, an amnesiac who wakes in a bizarre, rundown sanitarium. Lest you think this is a game about exploring a slightly eerie rundown hospital, let me disabuse you of that notion immediately: For fear of spoiling everything, I can only say: this game goes places. Richard Cobbett wrote about Sanitarium in his Crapshoot column , and Alexis Ong even went as far as to track down its creators . If you've played Sanitarium—especially divorced from its mid '90s context—you're probably evangelical about it. It carefully balances the line between camp and psychologically gruelling, but questions of tone aside, it's a gorgeously vivid and varied thing, with beautifully rendered isometric environments.
